an8.8:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Uttara was dwelling at Mahisavatthu, in Dhavajālikā on Mount Saṅkheyya.
an8.8:1.2: There the Venerable Uttara addressed the bhikkhus….
an8.8:1.3: “Friends, it is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review his own failings.
an8.8:1.4: It is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review the failings of others.
an8.8:1.5: It is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review his own achievements.
an8.8:1.6: It is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review the achievements of others.”
an8.8:2.1: Now on that occasion the great deva king Vessavaṇa was traveling from north to south on some business.
an8.8:2.2: He heard the Venerable Uttara at Mahisavatthu, in Dhavajālikā on Mount Saṅkheyya, teaching the Dhamma to the bhikkhus thus:
an8.8:2.3: ‘Friends, it is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review his own failings …
an8.8:3.1: Then, just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, Vessavaṇa disappeared from Mount Saṅkheyya and reappeared among the Tāvatiṁsa devas.
an8.8:3.2: He approached Sakka, ruler of the devas, and said to him:
an8.8:3.3: “Respected sir, you should know that the Venerable Uttara,
an8.8:3.4: at Mahisavatthu, in Dhavajālikā on Mount Saṅkheyya, has been teaching the Dhamma to the bhikkhus thus:
an8.8:3.5: ‘Friends, it is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review his own failings …
an8.8:4.1: Then, just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, Sakka disappeared from among the Tāvatiṁsa devas and reappeared at Mahisavatthu, in Dhavajālikā on Mount Saṅkheyya, in front of the Venerable Uttara.
an8.8:4.2: He approached the Venerable Uttara, paid homage to him, stood to one side, and said to him:
an8.8:5.1: “Is it true, Bhante, as is said, that you have been teaching the Dhamma to the bhikkhus thus:
an8.8:5.2: ‘Friends, it is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review his own failings …
an8.8:5.7: “But, Bhante, was this your own discernment, or was it the word of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One?”
an8.8:5.8: “Well then, ruler of the devas, I will give you a simile;
an8.8:5.9: even by means of a simile, some intelligent people understand the meaning of what has been said.
an8.8:6.1: Suppose not far from a village or town there was a great heap of grain,
an8.8:6.2: and a large crowd of people were to take away grain with carrying-poles,
an8.8:6.3: baskets, hip-sacks, and their cupped hands.
an8.8:6.4: If someone were to approach that large crowd of people and ask them:
an8.8:6.5: ‘Where did you get this grain?’ what should they say?”
an8.8:6.6: “Bhante, those people should say: ‘We got it from that great heap of grain.’”
an8.8:6.7: “So too, ruler of the devas, whatever is well spoken is all the word of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
an8.8:6.8: I myself and others derive our good words from him.”
an8.8:7.3: ‘Whatever is well spoken is all the word of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
an8.8:7.4: I myself and others derive our good words from him.’
an8.8:7.5: “On one occasion, Bhante Uttara, the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Mount Vulture Peak, not long after Devadatta had left.
an8.8:7.6: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus with reference to Devadatta:
an8.8:8.1: ‘Bhikkhus, it is good for a bhikkhu from time to time to review his own failings….
an8.8:10.1: Sakka here cites the Buddha’s entire discourse of 8:7,
an8.8:12.10: It is in such a way, bhikkhus, that you should train yourselves.’
an8.8:13.1: “Bhante Uttara, this exposition of the Dhamma has not been promulgated anywhere among the four human assemblies: that is, among bhikkhus,
an8.8:13.2: bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, and female lay followers.
an8.8:13.4: Bhante, learn this exposition of the Dhamma,
an8.8:13.5: master this exposition of the Dhamma,
an8.8:13.6: and retain this exposition of the Dhamma in mind.
an8.8:13.7: This exposition of the Dhamma is beneficial; it pertains to the fundamentals of the spiritual life.”
